products.summary: A handheld scanner with two light sources. The blue laser handles dark and shiny car parts. The infrared mode covers a 1,170 × 1,385 mm area from up to 1,400 mm away for engine bays and body panels. Wi-Fi and a swappable battery are built in.
products.fit: Car owners and fabricators who scan both large areas (engine bays, bumpers, fenders) and medium parts, and who already have a gaming-class Windows laptop or a recent Apple Silicon Mac.
caveats: Needs a strong computer: EINSTAR recommends an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop GPU or better and 32 GB of RAM. Only NVIDIA cards are supported on Windows.
Laser mode tracks only on stick-on markers. Plan to mark smooth parts.
EINSTAR lists no accuracy figure, only resolution (0.05 mm in laser mode).
Recent owner forum threads report EXStar Hub crashes and Wi-Fi connection trouble.
The store's free shipping starts at $1,000, so the scanner alone may pay shipping.

products.summary: EINSTAR's step-up hybrid scanner. Its crossed blue laser can track on the part's own shape, so many parts need no markers. It keeps the same 1,400 mm infrared reach for large areas.
products.fit: Shops and serious hobbyists who scan many shiny or machined parts and don't want to apply markers every time.
caveats: Costs $645 more than the EINSTAR 2 at today's store prices.
Needs at least 32 GB of RAM and an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop GPU; EINSTAR recommends 64 GB.
EINSTAR lists no accuracy figure, only resolution (0.05 mm in laser mode).
Owner forum threads mention uneven projected laser lines between units and Wi-Fi pairing trouble.

products.summary: A scanner with its own screen and computer, so you can scan a car in a driveway with no laptop attached. It is infrared-only, so dark or shiny parts are harder than with a blue-laser scanner.
products.fit: People who scan away from their desk or don't own a gaming laptop, and who mostly scan medium-to-large shapes rather than shiny machined parts.
caveats: No laser mode, so it is weaker on dark, shiny or finely detailed parts than the EINSTAR 2.
Heavier than the EINSTAR 2 (535 g vs 420 g).
The largest group of recent threads in EINSTAR's Issues forum concerns the VEGA (8 of 30): drivers, USB and Wi-Fi connection.

notes: Query choice: '3d scanner for car parts' and its variants. Results today are mostly thin affiliate roundups (abramsartists, bestcadpapers, thetoolstrunk, thewearify), vendor blogs (einstar.com, 3d-scantech) and Reddit threads. Pain points, counted by source: (1) PC/GPU demands, 4 sources: HP Academy 'insufficient memory' on 16 GB with the original Einstar; Reddit van-panel thread saying Einstar needs an NVIDIA GPU (search snippet); a Reddit user recommending the Raptor over Einstar for lower-end hardware (snippet); EINSTAR's own 32 GB / RTX 3060 recommendation. (2) Dark, shiny or featureless surfaces and markers, 5 sources: thetoolstrunk guide, Zelpio black-part test, HP Academy (Moose missed black brackets), EINSTAR forum thread 'Einstar 2 and black parts' (title only, Feb 2026, about 1,956 views, content not read), Reddit snippet on large smooth panels needing markers. (3) Software crashes or slow processing: 8 of the 30 latest EINSTAR Issues forum threads (6 crash/error + 2 performance); EINSTAR 2-tagged threads include an 0x00000012 crash, a performance drop after V1.51, a macOS 26.2 crash and Wi-Fi trouble. (4) Wireless connection: 5 of 30. (5) Weak on small objects (Einstar): UMAX, plus a Reddit snippet. Segment winners: large areas (engine bay, panels) on a budget = EINSTAR 2 (longest IR reach, 1,400 mm, and largest IR frame, 1,170 × 1,385 mm, among the sub-$900 options; the only one with Wi-Fi built in; also has a blue laser). Small precise parts = Creality Otter (0.017 mm in Zelpio) or Raptor (0.022 mm, sharpest text); neither brand is an approved program, so they appear as maker-link rows with Creality US store prices read today via storecheck (Otter $899, Raptor $879, Scan Bridge $279). Markerless laser = EINSTAR Rockit. No PC = EINSTAR VEGA (Revopoint MIRACO is the other standalone option; not compared or priced). Store data: EINSTAR prices were read on 2026-11-11 through storecheck search on www.einstar.com (EINSTAR 2 $854, compare-at $1,648; Rockit $1,499, compare-at $2,298; VEGA $1,499, compare-at $1,999; all available). storecheck 'product' and WebFetch of the product pages returned HTTP 429 every time. So the variant breakdown is unverified (the $854 may be the lowest variant), and I left out list_price because the compare-at figures may be bundle prices. The EINSTAR 2 battery count is unverified: the spec table lists one 5,500 mAh battery, but the FAQ says two batteries and a charger. Wi-Fi 6 is claimed only by resellers; the page says 'built-in Wi-Fi'. EINSTAR publishes no accuracy figure for the EINSTAR 2, Rockit or VEGA, only resolution or point distance. I found no independent measured test of the EINSTAR 2 itself; the HP Academy results are for the original Einstar, and the page says so. The Otter reach (120–1,200 mm) and the Raptor's approximate 170–1,000 mm come from Creality's UK comparison guide; retailers list 110–1,000 mm (Otter) and 150–400 mm (Raptor, mode unclear). Free shipping on einstar.com starts at $1,000 (cart widget); the US shipping cost for the EINSTAR 2 alone was not checked. No discount code was visible on einstar.com pages today. EINSTARSAS has not been cart-tested. Refurbished units are also sold (EINSTAR 2 $799, Rockit $1,399, VEGA $999) with a 6-month warranty; they are not recorded. No Amazon records, per the temporary rule.
